title: DIY AI Video Ads vs Done-for-You: True Cost
summary: Compare DIY AI video ads with a service using total software, labor and review cost per accepted ad. Use your own output rate, not credits alone, to decide.
body_markdown:
## When is DIY the better fit?


Consider DIY when your team wants hands-on control, can do the creative and review work, and can justify the time against other priorities. Our[in-house, agency and platform comparison](https://knowlify.com/articles/video-agency-vs-in-house-vs-ai-platform) helps define those responsibilities.


An occasional internal campaign may not need a continuing service commitment. An experienced editor may already have an efficient process. A team exploring a new format may benefit from direct experimentation before writing a larger production brief.


Keep a simple time log and accepted-output record for a representative batch. Decide whether the activity fits the team’s role instead of automatically assigning a high or low value to internal labor to make one option win.


## How do you value internal time without biasing the comparison?


Show cash outlay and allocated labor as separate totals. A salaried employee's time is not a new vendor invoice, but it is still time that cannot be used for another assigned task. The appropriate value depends on your planning question. A cash-constrained founder may focus first on immediate expense; a staffed marketing team may focus on capacity and work delayed elsewhere.


Use a consistent labor assumption on both sides. If you value DIY scriptwriting and review, also value the client time required to brief and approve a service. If you exclude salaried time to understand cash needs, label the result as cash cost rather than full production cost. Avoid selecting a high rate for DIY and a zero rate for service review merely to favor outsourcing.


For an illustrative team, one employee might spend five hours on creative and another spend two hours reviewing it. Record the two roles separately when their responsibilities or costs differ. Also distinguish active work from unattended processing. Waiting overnight for a render affects delivery timing, but it is not eight hours of hands-on labor unless someone really was occupied throughout.


Track displaced work with a concrete example. If producing a batch delays a planned landing-page revision, record that tradeoff without assigning fictional lost revenue. It may be enough to know that the team's agreed priority is repeatedly postponed. That makes the operating decision visible without pretending to calculate an exact return on every hour.


## What should a two-cycle production comparison include?


Use one initial batch and one follow-up batch as a proposed evaluation. The first tests whether the workflow can produce acceptable work from a new brief. The second tests whether the team can use feedback and repeat the process. Two cycles are an editorial suggestion for evaluating repeatability, not a statistically validated benchmark or a guarantee about vendor performance.


For a hypothetical meal-preparation product, the first batch could explain portion organization using approved footage. The second could address a different practical objection identified in customer conversations. Keep product claims and permissions consistent, while changing the message intentionally. Do not call a color change a new concept merely to increase the apparent output.


In DIY, record which templates, scripts or assets reduced effort in the second cycle. In the service route, record whether the provider retained the approved context and whether feedback reached the right person. If either route repeats a corrected error, describe that event and the remedy rather than turning one incident into a universal conclusion.


Decision First cycle Follow-up cycle


Creative direction Can the team turn the brief into a coherent concept? Can it apply a new learning without losing approved facts?


Production Can the required format pass review? Can the process repeat within the planned capacity?


Corrections Are mistakes identifiable and repairable? Are earlier corrections preserved?


Handoff Are usable files and responsibilities clear? Does feedback inform the next brief?


The result may favor a hybrid arrangement. Your team could retain research and early concept exploration while delegating finishing, or keep an internal buyer while outsourcing production. Assign the handoff explicitly; otherwise a hybrid can duplicate work without removing the original bottleneck.


## How should campaign management change the comparison?


Run a second responsibility comparison after the production comparison. Software used to create a video does not by itself assign someone to choose Meta campaign actions. Likewise, a production-only contract should not be assumed to include campaign management. Identify the owner of launch approval, account changes, spend decisions and reporting before considering the plan complete.


Knowlify offers end-to-end Meta ads that combine creative production and campaign management, as well as creative-only work for an existing buyer. Pricing is provided privately and media spend is separate. Match the quote to your desired ownership model rather than adding an agency-management assumption to the software budget without naming the work involved.


Keep measurement dependencies visible. Your business should explain what it can currently observe, which business outcome matters and who controls any systems outside the ad account. Do not infer tracking implementation, CRM management or support for additional channels from a creative-and-Meta proposal. If those are required, resolve them in a separate scope before launch.


Finish the decision with a written operating plan: who supplies product truth, who produces, who approves, who manages Meta and who decides what to make next. The cost worksheet becomes useful when it prices that actual plan. Without it, “DIY versus done-for-you” remains an incomplete comparison between a software invoice and a service promise.


## When should you use a done-for-you service?


Consider a service when you want defined production work owned by an external team and the proposed formats fit your message. Knowlify’s[video ad production](https://knowlify.com/video-ad-production) and[creative subscription](https://knowlify.com/creative-as-a-service) cover concept-to-render work, including[AI UGC](https://knowlify.com/ai-ugc-ads) , character animation and AI commercials.


Compare the proposal with the same acceptance criteria used for DIY. Include your own briefing and review time, confirm revision rules, and establish who handles campaign findings. A service does not remove the need for a client to approve product truth and brand requirements.


[Book a Knowlify call](https://knowlify.com/book) to receive pricing privately for the agreed scope. Evaluate the proposal against your measured workflow rather than an assumed universal quality or cost advantage.


## Key takeaways


- Software access and accepted output are different buying units.
- Include concept, editing and review time.
- Treat illustrative cost figures as assumptions, not results.
- Apply the same[production acceptance criteria](https://knowlify.com/articles/ai-video-production-company) to both options.


## FAQ


### Are AI credits equivalent to finished videos?


Do not assume so. Check the selected model and action costs, then measure how many attempts become accepted finished ads under your own production requirements.


### Is a done-for-you service always cheaper?


No. Compare a real quote with your measured software and labor costs for equivalent work. Include the client review time that remains even when production is outsourced.


### Can I combine DIY tools with a service?


Yes, if responsibilities are clear. Your team might supply approved assets or experiments while the service handles defined production work. Agree the handoff and rights before relying on those inputs.


### What work stays with my team when I outsource production?


Your team still needs to provide accurate product information, approve claims and creative direction, and review the finished ads. Assign someone to share campaign feedback for the next batch. Knowlify can own Meta campaign management together with creative production, or deliver creative-only work to your buyer. The agreement should name campaign and reporting responsibilities; pricing is private and media spend is separate.


### Should I include employee time in the cost of DIY AI ads?


Show it separately from cash expense. Record the hours spent on concepts, scripts, generation, editing and review, and use a clearly labeled labor assumption if you need a full-cost model. Apply the same method to client briefing and approval time for a service. This keeps the comparison useful without pretending employee time is a supplier invoice.
